mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate (below 3.0%) signals an accommodative monetary policy that reduces discount rates for equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When FEDFUNDS is below 3.0%, the 20-day forward returns of SPX are negative in more than 60% of cases over the walk-forward period.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 5.0% indicates deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate earnings, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: When UNRATE exceeds 5.0%, the 5-day forward returns of SPX are positive in more than 60% of cases over the walk-forward period.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts and retail sales (both >0.5% in one month) signal a sharp contraction in consumer demand, which triggers negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS decline > 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: When both HOUST and RSAFS decline > 0.5% in 1 month, the 60-day forward returns of SPX are positive in more than 60% of cases over the walk-forward period.

mechanism_narrative: In a recession (defined by GDPC1 decline from prior quarter), a decline in industrial production indicates worsening economic activity, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods when GDPC1 declines from prior quarter, a decline in INDPRO leads to positive 20-day forward returns in more than 60% of cases over the walk-forward period.

mechanism_narrative: Strong non-farm payroll growth (positive monthly change) reflects a robust labor market that supports consumer spending and corporate profits, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: When PAYEMS growth is positive, the 5-day forward returns of SPX are negative in more than 60% of cases over the walk-forward period.

mechanism_narrative: High annualized inflation (CPIAUCSL > 2.5%) signals potential monetary tightening, which increases real interest rates and reduces equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: When CPIAUCSL annualized inflation exceeds 2.5%, the 60-day forward returns of SPX are positive in more than 60% of cases over the walk-forward period.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent declines in housing starts (HOUST) and quarterly GDP growth (GDPC1) indicate a severe demand slowdown, which leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST decline > 0.5% in 1 month and GDPC1 decline from prior quarter
failure_condition: When HOUST declines > 0.5% in 1 month and GDPC1 declines from prior quarter, the 20-day forward returns of SPX are positive in more than 60% of cases over the walk-forward period.

mechanism_narrative: A monetary tightening cycle (FEDFUNDS rising) increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate investment, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods when FEDFUNDS is rising, the 60-day forward returns of SPX are positive in more than 60% of cases over the walk-forward period.
